newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cordovez says leakage of UN text hurt Cyprus talks.
newsitem.headline: Cordovez says leakage of UN text hurt Cyprus talks.

text.p: United Nations mediator Diego Cordovez said on Friday that talks on Cyprus unity would continue and he had accepted an invitation from both sides to visit Nicosia, but added no date was set for the next session.

Cordovez, speaking after five days of meetings between Greek Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash near Montreux, said he would meet on Monday with officials from Britain, which this month holds the Security Council presidency.
He said he would report to the full 15-member Security Council in New York on Wednesday.

Cordovez, a former Ecuador foreign minister, also said he would meet in New York on Wednesday with Richard Holbrooke, U.S. President Bill Clinton's diplomatic troubleshooter who has a Cyprus brief. "We will coordinate our actions," he said.

Cordovez, visibly annoyed during a final news conference in Montreux after the talks ended without a breakthrough, said that the leakage of his latest U.N. draft proposals had damaged the negotiating process.
The first round was held in July in Troutbeck, New York.
Earlier, Clerides and Denktash -- speaking at separate news conferences -- blamed each other for the lack of progress.
Clerides threatened to pull out of negotiations with Turkish Cypriots if the European Union (EU) delayed the Cyprus entry talks set for early 1998.

He said of the U.N. statement: "There were at least 10 different drafts of the statement which Mr Cordovez wanted to make. At least half of them Mr Denktash objected to and I objected to the other half."

Denktash said that the Greek Cypriots had blocked an agreement by refusing to give Turks sovereign equality on the divided island. In the meantime, he said, the EU threw in a bombshell with a decision to start entry talks early next year for the Greek Cypriot government.
But Cordovez, who was foreign minister of Ecuador from 1988 to 1992, put on a brave face on the lack of tangible progress.
He said the two sides were less far apart on some issues than they admitted, but declined to be specific.
"I believe that the two leaders remain committed to achieving a settlement of the Cyprus problem on the basis of which over time a bizonal, bicommunal federation will be established," Cordovez said.
"Their personal relationship is good and remains good and this helps," he added. "I tell them that on many issues they are not as far apart as they believe."
The discussions -- conducted during a media blackout -- had been "very useful". "We will proceed on that basis," he added.
Cordovez strongly criticised leakage of his latest document leaked to the Greek Cypriot press this week. Asked whether the leak had damaged the talks, he replied: "Yes."
"We cannot negotiate publicy. I don't like to negotiate through the press," he added. "I regret the fact that you know the existence of these documents."
He gave few details about the statement which the two leaders had said he was expected to issue.

"The problem about the poor intermediary and good offices of the United Nations is that each side wants to put in something of interest to his side. The person in the middle can only make a general statement or only parts of statements acceptable to them," Cordovez said.
After the news conference, a U.N. spokesman said there would be no final written U.N. statement. "What you heard is what you get," he told reporters.
